title: Giant magnetoelasticity in FeRh thin films evidenced via strong phonon-magnon coupling
authors: D. Ourdani, C. Gourdon, J. A. Arregi, V. Uhlíř, Y. Roussigné, and L. Thevenard
abstract:
Author(s): D. Ourdani, C. Gourdon, J. A. Arregi, V. Uhlíř, Y. Roussigné, and L. Thevenard

FeRh is best known for its metamagnetic transition and giant volume magnetostriction. Here, the authors reveal remarkably strong phonon–magnon coupling in epitaxial FeRh. Combining Brillouin light scattering experiments with magnetoacoustic modeling, they demonstrate giant magnetoelasticity and show that Love surface acoustic waves provide an efficient mechanism for coherent magnon-polaron formation in magnetic thin films, highlighting FeRh as a promising platform for spin-acoustic information processing.

Here, the authors report the magnetic properties, crystal electric field excitations, and spin dynamics of a distorted honeycomb magnet BiErGeO5. Inelastic neutron scattering and μSR experiments reveal the effect of crystal electric field leading to a Kramers doublet ground state and anisotropic interactions. Despite an anomaly at TN ≃ 0.4 K in heat capacity, μSR measurements rule out a magnetic long-range order, and instead suggest persistent spin fluctuations down to 30 mK, highlighting unconventional magnetism in this spin-orbit coupled honeycomb system.

Here, the authors show that this variability can arise from microscopic parameters: the systematic exploration of the phase diagram reveals that twist angle θ, filling, and interlayer tunneling strength stabilize distinct competing superconducting states.
